..summary: markdown_to_html is independently implemented in three modules (markdown_to_pdf/utils.py, html_website/utils.py, lab_manual/utils.py) instead of being shared

evidence: markdown_to_pdf/utils.py lines 11-32: markdown.Markdown(extensions=['extra','codehilite','tables','fenced_code'])
html_website/utils.py lines 11-21: markdown.Markdown(extensions=['extra','codehilite','tables']) — omits 'fenced_code'
lab_manual/utils.py imports markdown and invokes it inline in its own markdown_to_html (confirmed by lab_manual/main.py importing markdown_to_html from .utils)
Three diverged implementations; a developer adding an extension must update three files
detail.suggestion: Consolidate into src/shared/markdown_utils.py with a single markdown_to_html(text, extensions=None) that defaults to the full extension list. The html_website variant's omission of 'fenced_code' can be passed as an optional override. All three modules import from the shared location.

..summary: Five validate_X_name functions in file_validation/utils.py are pure aliases for matches_pattern with a config constant — a three-hop wrapper chain with no added policy

evidence: validate_assignment_name(file_name) at line 71 returns matches_pattern(file_name, config.ASSIGNMENT_PATTERN)
validate_lecture_name, validate_lab_name, validate_study_guide_name, validate_quiz_name follow the same pattern (lines 83, 95, 107, 119)
matches_pattern itself (line 33) is just bool(pattern.match(name))
Call chain from any caller: caller -> validate_X_name -> matches_pattern -> pattern.match — three hops with no policy added at any intermediate step
detail.suggestion: Inline the pattern match at the call site, or replace all five with a single get_file_type(name) that switches on config patterns directly. If individual validators are needed for external readability, collapse the intermediate matches_pattern layer so each validate_X_name does bool(config.X_PATTERN.match(file_name)) directly.

..summary: generate_measurement_table in lab_manual/main.py is a public-API stub that forwards all parameters unchanged to create_measurement_table_html in utils.py

evidence: lab_manual/main.py lines 152-177: generate_measurement_table(rows, aspects, include_device, include_unit, include_value) returns create_measurement_table_html(rows=rows, aspects=aspects, include_device=include_device, include_unit=include_unit, include_value=include_value)
Identical signatures; no pre-processing, validation, defaulting, or logging added
Scan confirms: pass_through_wrappers entry for lab_manual/main.py: generate_measurement_table->create_measurement_table_html
detail.suggestion: Either re-export create_measurement_table_html directly from main.py under the public name, or fold the public function's name onto the util directly. If the separation of main/utils is the convention, add at least a MeasurementConfig construction step in main.py to mirror how generate_data_table builds a TableConfig before delegating.

..summary: configure_voice_settings() exists purely for completeness; all three parameters are documented as unused with gTTS

evidence: Lines 101-123: docstring explicitly states voice, speed, and pitch are 'currently not used with gTTS'. The function body only clamps values and copies config, with no path that affects actual TTS output.
detail.suggestion: Remove the function or collapse it to a comment/TODO until a TTS engine that supports these parameters is actually adopted.

..summary: Multi-line docstrings on trivial 1-3 line utility functions in batch_processing/utils.py

evidence: find_markdown_files (body: return find_files(directory, [...]) — one line) carries a 6-line docstring.
find_audio_files (body: return find_files(directory, [...]) — one line) carries a 6-line docstring.
get_relative_output_path (body: two assignments) carries an 8-line docstring.
should_process_file (body: for loop with conditional return, 3 lines) carries an 8-line docstring.
detail.suggestion: Replace multi-line docstrings on these trivial functions with single-line docstrings; the function name and type signature already convey the intent.

..summary: format_conversion/utils.py convert_markdown_to_pdf() does nothing except call render_markdown_to_pdf with str() casts

evidence: Lines 43-50: the entire body is render_markdown_to_pdf(str(input_path), str(output_path)). No policy, logging, or translation is added.
detail.suggestion: Eliminate the wrapper; callers can call render_markdown_to_pdf directly or perform the str() cast at the call site.

..summary: format_conversion/main.py get_conversion_path() is a pure pass-through with no added logic

evidence: Lines 143-154: function imports _get_conversion_path from .utils and immediately returns its result with no transformation, validation, or policy.
detail.suggestion: Delete the wrapper and have callers import directly from format_conversion.utils, or inline the utility if it is simple enough.

..summary: Inline comments throughout batch_processing/main.py restate what the immediately following code does

evidence: '# Find all Markdown files' above find_markdown_files() call.
'# Filter out files in skip directories' above list comprehension filtering skip dirs.
'# Get output path maintaining structure' above get_relative_output_path() call.
'# Ensure output directory exists' above ensure_output_directory() call.
'# Convert to PDF' above render_markdown_to_pdf() call.
These appear repeatedly across process_module_to_pdf, process_module_to_audio, and process_module_to_text.
detail.suggestion: Delete comments that only repeat the function name. Retain only comments explaining non-obvious constraints (e.g., the time.sleep(2) comment explaining 429 rate-limit avoidance is a good example to keep).

..summary: Six-format try/except dispatch block is copy-pasted verbatim between process_module_by_type and process_syllabus

evidence: Lines 382-463 in process_module_by_type and lines 534-615 in process_syllabus contain structurally identical per-format try/except blocks: error_msg = f'<Format> generation failed for {md_file.name}: {e}', logger.error(error_msg, exc_info=True), results[key].append(error_msg).
Each of the six formats (pdf, mp3, docx, html, txt, md) repeats the same three-line error pattern with only the format name changed.
detail.suggestion: Extract a _render_format(md_file, fmt, output_path, results, key) helper that handles the try/except and result accumulation; call it from both process_module_by_type and process_syllabus.

..summary: Sibling batch functions return List[str] in most modules but Dict with 'files'+'errors' in lab_manual

evidence: batch_render_markdown(...) -> List[str]
batch_generate_speech(...) -> List[str]
batch_transcribe_audio(...) -> List[str]
batch_render_lab_manuals(...) -> Dict[str, Any]  (keys: 'files', 'errors')
detail.suggestion: Either adopt the richer Dict shape for all batch functions (providing error details alongside successes), or flatten batch_render_lab_manuals to List[str] to match siblings. The Dict shape is arguably better — standardize on it across all batch functions.
